### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **54** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac7b9d80c7fb7e213b5999416eddd74bb7b4b587`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **67** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac7b9d80c7fb7e213b5999416eddd74bb7b4b587` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0facc50e95137af86bc69c108c68bd804a36836a` — the merge of head `caf6941d896ed4f833d24f15b5ecf995ca45be47` into base `ac7b9d80c7fb7e213b5999416eddd74bb7b4b587`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0facc50e95137af86bc69c108c68bd804a36836a && git checkout 0facc50e95137af86bc69c108c68bd804a36836a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ac7b9d80c7fb7e213b5999416eddd74bb7b4b587 caf6941d896ed4f833d24f15b5ecf995ca45be47 && git checkout -B drift-repro ac7b9d80c7fb7e213b5999416eddd74bb7b4b587 && git merge --no-ff caf6941d896ed4f833d24f15b5ecf995ca45be47

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac7b9d80c7fb7e213b5999416eddd74bb7b4b587
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ac7b9d80c7fb7e213b5999416eddd74bb7b4b587` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a9779e0f16e087671077c0d3d53fcc4d89095004`
Local-runs: probe — one worktree at the head (closure built with OS_SKIP_DTS=1): the touched packages' targeted suites, one ablation of the late-install re-judge, and uncommitted scratch cases to confirm the door and store findings before grading them
Scope: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts (+test), packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts (+match-endpoint test), packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, picklist-resolution.ts, plugin.ts, registry.ts and their picklist / boot-audit / exact-qualifier / bare-name-one-holder family tests, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts (+dataset-holders test), index.ts, protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-qualified-item-read.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references.integration.test.ts, the two dogfood family tests + read for context: database-loader.ts, memory-loader.ts, protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, package-scoped-read.ts, engine-hooks-and-functions.ts, metadata-facade.ts

### ① Derived judgments
- Declaration lines match rulings 6810963021: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` in the body and the changeset, with the ADR-0087 marker.
- Probe at head: objectql family + picklist files 348/348; core package-scoped-resolution 29/29; metadata match-endpoint 412/412; metadata-protocol build-probes-dataset-holders 7/7. Not run locally: runtime, cli, dogfood.
- Ablation: with the late-install refusal in `plugin.ts` disabled, both ruling-A order pins go red and the two CONTROLs stay green; restored, 68/68.
- Ruling A (6811306558) holds for the two pinned orders. `findPicklistReferencesBrokenBy` judges the pending view before `registerApp`, the refusal names each reference and both holders, and the tests assert nothing registered.
- Red line 3 (reads): one-holder bare names read as before; the store's one-holder CONTROL covers picklist, mapping and dataset.
- `function` is exempted by name in exactly two pins (slotted superset, exact-qualifier 501); `claimBareNameFunctions` reads the incoming namespace from the installed record.
- Three scratch cases contradict the PR's claims; they are must-fix 1–3 below.

### ② Semver level
`minor` on core, metadata, objectql and metadata-protocol is right for `narrowed`. The BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker are present. runtime, cli and dogfood change tests only.

### ③ Boundary flags
- No `packages/spec` file and no governed path in the diff.
- `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__bare-name-one-holder.ts.json` still names only agent and skill as narrowed. It is outside the diff; flagged for its owner.
- Landing after #32214 and #31696 PR-3 means a new head: the three type sets and these pins are re-reviewed there.
- mapping, dataset and function have no install-door re-judge. A late second holder makes a dependent's read answer 409 naming both at use time: reported, not guessed. Noted, not graded.

### ④ Design judgment
The narrowing does what ADR-0150 D2/D9 says on the pinned paths, and fails on these:

**Must-fix**
1. **Self-extension slips the late-install door.** `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:1016` (`if (own.has(ref.picklist)) return undefined;`, applied to extensions at `:1029`) and `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:10532` skip the incoming package's own extensions. Measured: alpha holds `p1`, and a late install of gamma declaring `p1` plus a `picklistExtensions` entry on `p1` is admitted (main: refused `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`). `findOrphanPicklistExtensions()` then names gamma's extension, and the next cold boot is refused. This breaks ruling A and row 7's "refused at install". Needs a late-order pin.
2. **A late install can silently strip an installed field's options.** `registry.ts:10495` judges each referrer alone; `plugin.ts:1329` names the disagreement only at boot. Measured: alpha owns `alpha_item.s → p1`. A late install or upgrade of gamma that declares its own `p1` and redeclares that field in `objectExtensions` is admitted; served options go from `['alpha_one']` to `[]` with no error and no log. This is the harm ruling A was made for, on another package's field (red line 2).
3. **Undeclared moved answers** (red line 3). `package-slotted-store.ts:111` moves the store contract for picklist, mapping and dataset; the changeset declares only rows 4–6:
   - (a) `unregister(type, NAME, { packageId })` naming a non-holder: FROM item removed TO nothing removed (one-holder move).
   - (b) `unregisterPackage(holder)` after a package-less write over its name: FROM package-less item stays TO removed with the slot (one-holder move).
   - (c) `list(type)` for a two-holder name: FROM the survivor alone TO both (#32151 declared the same line for agent/skill, plus the realtime event kind).
   - (d) A package-less write under a two-holder name: FROM replacing the stored item TO a bare slot, listed, answered by no by-name read.
   - (e) DatabaseLoader for these types: one row per (package, name) with `package_id`, a no-package delete of a two-holder name refused, and rollback by name refused when several slots exist (read, not measured).
   - (f) `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts:163`: a bare read on a registry with `readsByPackage(type) === false`: FROM served TO `501`.
   Each needs a FROM → TO row with its Clause-② arm in the body and changeset, and a pin where none iterates the new types ((a), (b), (e)).

**Should-fix**
- Item seam: `registry.registerItem('picklist', …, 'com.acme.beta')` after seal is admitted beside an installed extension (one orphan measured). Moving the re-judge into the registry closes it with must-fix 1.
- Hot reload: `plugin.ts:1866` re-registers through `registerApp` and bypasses the door. Declare it or cover it.
- Bare engine function read: `ObjectQL#resolveFunction` / `resolveFunctionEntry` (`engine-hooks-and-functions.ts:270-276`) answer the last-registered function, now that two namespaces' holders are admitted.
- `Skills-docs:` should read `follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`; the line names `SKILL.md:261` as now false.
- Row 12: state that a widget's dataset held outside the publishing package's closure goes FROM probed TO `widget_not_probed`.

**Nits**: the reworded `describeUnresolvedPicklistReferences` sentence is in the body but not the changeset; the dev report counts 21 build-probe tests where the touched file holds 7.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-du44hj`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYGYEUhpi29FpjLmxT`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2386ae1a868bfb0a7833e4320cddae0564d80674`
Local-runs: probe — one worktree at the head (closures built with OS_SKIP_DTS=1): the touched suites, one ablation of `judgePicklistArrival`, one revert of the three store types, and uncommitted scratch cases for the round-1 findings, the R2-A seams and the R2-C caller
Scope: delta over FAIL 6812847136 at a9779e0f per epic ruling 6812862622: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, plugin.ts, picklist-resolution.ts, engine.ts, engine-registration.ts, engine-hooks-and-functions.ts and their family / boot-audit / resolver / hook-binder tests, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains tests + read for context: packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/objectql/src/metadata-facade.ts

### ① Derived judgments
- **Declarations stand:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, ADR-0087 marker present. Size: 1876+ / 287−, 32 files.
- **Probe at head, all green:**
  - objectql family, picklist, resolver, hook-binder and engine: 766/766
  - core: 29/29
  - metadata match-endpoint: 484/484
  - metadata-protocol dataset-holders: 7/7
  - runtime (three files): 72/72
- **R2-A holds on every named path.** `SchemaRegistry.judgePicklistArrival` (`registry.ts:10762`) is reached from:
  - the install door
  - direct `registerApp`
  - hot reload
  - `registerItem('picklist')`
  - `registerPicklistExtension`
  - `registerObject`

  It judges one pending view, with no own-name shortcut.
  - The four round-1 cases and eleven new scratch cases are refused before anything registers, naming the reference and both holders.
  - CONTROL: a second namespace's list with its own field installs.
  - Ablation turns 13 pins red.
- **R2-B holds.** (a)–(f) are declared with arms; reverting the three store types turns 18 tests red.
- **R2-C is pinned (409 naming both, one-holder CONTROL), but row 19's "no production caller" is false at this head.** See must-fix 2.
- **R2-D:** row 12 and the nits are fixed. `Skills-docs:` still reads `follow-up owed`; the seat rewrites it to `follow-up #32522`.

### ② Semver level
`minor` on core, metadata, objectql and metadata-protocol is right for `narrowed`. Must-fix 2 adds a runtime source change and a changeset line.

### ③ Boundary flags
- No `packages/spec` file and no governed path.
- A stored row registered with no package argument but stamped with another namespace's `_packageId` is an unjudged second holder on `main` too. This is not this PR's move; it is a follow-up candidate.

### ④ Design judgment
**Must-fix**
1. **A tenant-authored list under a package skips the re-judge** (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:8186`, `type === 'picklist' && packageId && !isTenantAuthored(item)`).
   - What moves: `registerItem('picklist', { name: 'p1', _provenance: 'org' }, 'name', 'com.acme.beta')` after the seal, with alpha holding `p1` and gamma's installed extension of it, is admitted. `main` refused it 422.
   - Measured: alpha and beta become holders, and gamma's extension is orphaned silently.
   - Fix: judge any registration that fills a package's slot (an overlay of the holder's own list adds no holder and passes), and pin it.
2. **R2-C's refusal reaches a production caller** (`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts:548`, `bare: engine.resolveFunctionEntry?.(name)` in `releaseMovedFunctions`, from #32468).
   - What moves: a re-bind that moves one function off an owner which also keeps a two-namespace function name. Before: released and held once. Now: the bare read throws 409, teardown aborts with an error log, and the moved function stays held by both owners.
   - Measured: one-holder CONTROL clean.
   - Fix: read the owner's own entry for a name several packages hold, add a runtime pin, and correct row 19 in the body and the changeset.

**Should-fix**
- A refused hot reload still ingests the payload's objects (`plugin.ts:1435-1436`), so row 18's "refused whole" overstates. Skip the ingest on refusal, or reword the row.
- Row 12 moves a one-holder answer with the arm at "—"; give it its narrowing arm.
- `bind-database-loader-row-packages` now also binds picklist, mapping and dataset rows; say so in one changeset line.

## Epic red-line read at `2386ae1a86` · 2026-11-12T05:22Z

Head-sha: `2386ae1a868bfb0a7833e4320cddae0564d80674`

**No PASS.** Two findings, both measured in the contract review's probe at this head (must-fix 1 and 2 of the record above).

- **Red line 1 (resolution never loosened): holds.** Every packaged arrival after the seal meets `judgePicklistArrival` over one pending view. The round-1 cases and eleven further scratch cases are refused before anything registers, and ablating the judge turns 13 pins red.
- **Red line 2 (ambiguity reported, never guessed): broken on two paths.**
  - `registry.ts:8186`: a tenant-authored list under another namespace's package is admitted unjudged and silently orphans an installed extension. `main` refused it.
  - `app-artifact-handlers.ts:548`: the re-bind's bare `resolveFunctionEntry` throws for a two-namespace name, so the moved function stays held by two packages.
- **Red line 3 (independently releasable): not yet.**
  - One-holder answers are unchanged, with CONTROLs, and (a)–(f) are declared and pinned.
  - The two moves above are undeclared and unpinned, and row 19's "no production caller" is false after #32468.
